mainTopic: Dough in a kneading bowl and טומאה (אביי, רבא, רב פפא); deaf dough and the מיל measure; going four מילין for water; separating impure חלה on יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens by explaining the משנה's words 'and so too regarding טומאה' about dough stuck in a kneading bowl (עריבה). אביי says the dough combines with other impure food to reach a כביצה. רבא objects that the משנה says חוצץ, so he reads it as dough blocking the טבילה of an impure bowl. רב פפא objects that the משנה says טומאה, not טהרה, and concludes that the case is a שרץ touching the dough: does the impurity pass down to the bowl? In every reading the rule is the same. On פסח the dough's איסור makes it significant, and during the year it all depends on whether the owner is מקפיד. A new משנה then forbids 'deaf dough' if similar dough has become חמץ, and ריש לקיש teaches that without such dough the measure is the time of walking a מיל. The גמרא adds the four-מיל rule for finding water to wash before kneading, תפלה, and eating, notes a fourth case (tanning), and limits the rule when the water is behind the traveler. Finally a new משנה asks how to separate impure חלה on יום טוב, bringing the views of רבי אליעזר and בן בתירא. רבי יהושע's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי: the comparison is about combining for impurity
steps.stepSummary: The continuation of אביי's explanation: the משנה's 'וכן לענין טומאה' is about צירוף טומאה. On פסח the rule is fixed, but during the rest of the year there is a distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: [אביי explains:] Regarding combining for ritual impurity on פסח, it is one rule. During the rest of the year there is a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of אביי's explanation of the משנה's phrase 'and so too regarding טומאה.' He says it means combining food together for impurity, and that the rule differs between פסח and the rest of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads 'וכן' as linking two cases. On פסח the dough is treated one way, and during the year it is treated differently. The next step spells out the exact case he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Combining. Two small pieces join together to reach a minimum size.
Ritual impurity
The rest of the days of the year, outside of פסח
A distinction or division. Here it does not mean a dispute between two Sages.

steps.confusionAlert: Here פלוגתא does not mean that two Sages argue. It means that the law itself splits into two cases during the rest of the year.

phrases.english: regarding combining for ritual impurity on Pesach,
phrases.notes: This continues אביי's explanation, which began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: and during the rest of the year there is a distinction.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעִנְיַן צֵירוּף טוּמְאָה בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues אביי's reading of the משנה from the end of the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's phrase 'וכן לענין טומאה' refers to צירוף טומאה. The rule on פסח differs from the rule during the rest of the year.

steps.title: אביי's case: small impure food touches the dough
steps.stepSummary: אביי defines his case. Impure food smaller than a כביצה touches the dough in the bowl. On פסח the dough always joins to complete the כביצה. During the year it joins only if the owner is מקפיד on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? There is less than an egg-sized amount of impure food, and it touched this dough. On פסח, since the dough's prohibition makes it important, it combines. During the rest of the year, it depends on whether the owner minds it. If he minds it, it combines. If he wants it to stay, it is like part of the bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי spells out the exact situation he means and gives the rule for פסח and for the rest of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food needs to be at least a כביצה to pass on טומאה. On פסח the dough counts as real food because its איסור makes it important (חשוב), so it fills in the missing amount. During the year it counts as food only if the owner wants it gone. If he wants it to stay, it counts as part of the bowl and not as food.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
An egg's volume. This is the minimum amount of food that can pass on טומאה.
Its prohibition makes it significant
He minds it. He wants it removed.
He wants it to remain where it is
A kneading bowl

steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the key idea that whether the owner minds something (קפידא) decides whether it counts as a separate item or as part of the vessel.

phrases.english: What is the case?
For example, where there is less than an egg-bulk of [impure] food,
and it touched this dough.
On Pesach, since its prohibition makes it significant, it combines.
During the rest of the year,
when the matter depends on the owner's minding,
if he minds it, it combines;

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ — הֲרֵי הוּא כַּעֲרֵיבָה.
phrases.english: if he wants it to remain, it is like the kneading bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי, כְּגוֹן דְּאִיכָּא פָּחוֹת מִכְּבֵיצָה אוֹכָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This defines the exact case behind אביי's general statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פסח the dough always combines with the impure food to make a כביצה. During the year it combines only if the owner is מקפיד on it. Otherwise it counts as part of the bowl.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה says 'interposes,' not 'combines'
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי from the wording of the משנה. The משנה says 'חוצץ' (it blocks), not 'מצטרף' (it combines).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: Does the משנה say 'combines'? It says 'interposes'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation because it does not match the exact word used in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוצץ means something blocks contact, as in blocking water from reaching a vessel during טבילה. That is a different concept from food joining together to reach a size. So אביי's reading does not fit the משנה's own language.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
Does it teach...? A rhetorical challenge based on the wording.
Interposes or blocks. It is a barrier between water and the vessel.
Combines. It joins together to reach a minimum size.

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to this:
Does it teach 'combines'?
But it teaches 'interposes'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: מִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This rejects אביי's reading in steps 1 and 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that the משנה is about צירוף טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה uses the word חוצץ, which describes blocking, not combining. So אביי's reading contradicts the text.

steps.title: רבא's reading: purifying the bowl through immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers his own reading. 'וכן' refers to purifying the bowl, meaning the טבילה of an impure עריבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: And so too regarding bringing purity to the kneading bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected אביי's reading, רבא gives a new explanation of the משנה that fits the word 'חוצץ'. This sets up the case he describes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא changes the subject of the comparison. It is not about the dough making other things impure. It is about whether the dough blocks the bowl from becoming pure in a מקוה. That matches the word חוצץ perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This signals a new explanation that replaces the old one.
To bring purity, meaning to purify through טבילה

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
And so too regarding bringing purity to the kneading bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: וְכֵן לְהַעֲלוֹת טׇהֳרָה לַעֲרֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers רבא's own challenge by replacing אביי's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the subject of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about the dough combining to make a כביצה of impure food (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about the dough blocking the טבילה of an impure bowl, which matches the word חוצץ.

steps.title: רבא's case: the dough blocks the bowl's immersion
steps.stepSummary: An impure עריבה is being immersed. On פסח the dough always blocks the טבילה. During the year it blocks only if the owner is מקפיד. If he wants it to stay, it counts as part of the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? This kneading bowl became impure, and one wants to immerse it. On פסח, since the dough's prohibition makes it important, it interposes, and the immersion does not work. During the rest of the year, it depends on whether he minds it. If he minds it, it interposes. If he wants it to stay, it is like part of the bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא spells out the exact case behind his reading and gives the rule for פסח and for the rest of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything the owner wants removed counts as a barrier (חציצה) between the water and the vessel, so the טבילה fails. On פסח the dough is always important because of its איסור, so it always blocks. During the year, dough the owner is happy to leave becomes part of the bowl, and the טבילה works.

keyTerms.meaning: It became impure
To immerse in a מקוה
The immersion does not take effect for it

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the dough combines (מצטרף) with other food to make a כביצה. רבא: the dough blocks (חוצץ) the bowl's טבילה, which fits the משנה's word חוצץ. Both agree on the basic rule. On פסח the איסור makes the dough important. During the year it all depends on the owner's קפידא. רבא's reading is not final: the next step has רב פפא challenge it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case is a classic source for the rule that whether something counts as a חציצה depends on whether the owner minds it (מקפיד).

phrases.english: What is the case?
For example, where this kneading bowl became impure,
and he wants to immerse it.
On Pesach, since its prohibition makes it significant, it interposes,
and the immersion does not take effect for it.
During the rest of the year
the matter depends on the owner's minding.
If he minds it, it interposes;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ — הֲרֵי הוּא כַּעֲרֵיבָה.
phrases.english: and if he wants it to remain, it is like the kneading bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי, כְּגוֹן דְּאִיטַּמִּי הָךְ עֲרֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This defines the exact case behind רבא's new reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פסח the dough always blocks the טבילה of the bowl. During the year it blocks only if the owner is מקפיד. Otherwise it counts as part of the bowl, and the טבילה is valid.

steps.title: רב פפא objects that the משנה speaks of impurity, not purity
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא. The משנה says 'לענין טומאה', but רבא explained it as being about purifying the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: Does the משנה say 'and similarly regarding purity'? It says 'regarding impurity'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רבא's explanation of the משנה. רבא made the משנה about purifying the bowl, but the משנה's own word is 'טומאה', impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read 'וכן לענין טומאה' as being about the טבילה of an impure עריבה, which is a purification case. רב פפא says that bends the משנה's wording. A case about becoming pure would be called 'טהרה', not 'טומאה'. So the reading must be about something becoming impure.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it; introduces a challenge to the previous view
Does it (the משנה) teach...? A wording-based challenge
Purity / the process of becoming pure
Ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is attacking רבא's answer from Step 4, not אביי's. אביי was already rejected by רבא. Now רבא himself is being challenged, using the same kind of wording argument he used against אביי.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objected to it:
Does it teach 'and similarly regarding purity'?
phrases.notes: This describes רבא's reading, which is about טבילה.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'regarding impurity'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: מִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's explanation given in Steps 4–5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that 'וכן' refers to the טבילה (purification) of the עריבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'טומאה', so it cannot be describing a purification process.

steps.title: רב פפא's reading: impurity passing down to the bowl
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא offers his own reading. The משנה is about whether טומאה passes through the dough to the עריבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: 'And similarly regarding bringing impurity down to the kneading bowl.'
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבא's reading, רב פפא gives a new explanation that fits the word 'טומאה'. The question is whether the bowl becomes impure through the dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case the bowl was already impure and was being purified. In רב פפא's case the bowl starts out pure. The question is whether impurity reaches it through the dough. This keeps the משנה's word 'טומאה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new explanation that replaces the rejected one
To bring impurity down, meaning to transfer it onward
Kneading bowl or trough

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
And similarly regarding bringing impurity down to the kneading bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in Step 6 by offering a new reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וכן לענין טומאה' meant purifying an impure bowl (רבא).
steps.terutzMaskana: It means whether impurity is passed down through the dough into a pure bowl.

steps.title: The case: a creeping animal touches the dough in the bowl
steps.stepSummary: A שרץ touches the dough. On פסח the dough blocks, and the bowl stays pure. During the year it depends on whether the owner is מקפיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? A שרץ touched this dough. On פסח, when its prohibition makes it significant, it blocks, and the impurity does not go down to the bowl. During the rest of the year, when it depends on being particular: if he is particular about it, it blocks. If he wants it to stay, it is like the bowl itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא spells out the exact case his reading describes. He also explains the difference between פסח and the rest of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two outcomes are possible. If the dough is a separate item, the שרץ has touched only food, and the bowl is not made impure through it. If the dough counts as part of the bowl, then touching the dough is the same as touching the bowl, and the bowl becomes impure. On פסח the dough is a forbidden thing that must be removed, so it is always separate (חוצץ). During the year it is separate only if the owner is bothered by it (מקפיד). If he wants it there, it becomes part of the bowl.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? Introduces the exact scenario
Carcass of a creeping animal, a source of טֻמְאָה
Its prohibition makes it significant, so it counts as a separate item
It blocks or separates; here, it keeps the impurity from reaching the bowl
Particular about it; bothered by its presence
Wants it to remain

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חוצץ' is good for the bowl: it keeps the bowl pure. In רבא's case (Step 5), 'חוצץ' was bad for the bowl: it ruined the טבילה. The same word works in opposite directions in the two readings.
steps.whatToRemember: Final reading of 'וכן לענין טומאה' (רב פפא): On פסח the dough always separates, so the bowl stays pure. During the year, if he is מקפיד the bowl stays pure. If he wants the dough there, it counts as the bowl and the bowl becomes impure.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
For example, where a creeping animal touched this dough.
On Pesach, when its prohibition makes it significant,
it blocks, and the impurity does not go down to it (the bowl).
During the rest of the year, when it depends on being particular,
if he is particular about it, it blocks;

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ — הֲרֵי הוּא כַּעֲרֵיבָה.
phrases.english: if he wants it to remain, it is like the bowl itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי, כְּגוֹן דְּנָגַע שֶׁרֶץ בְּהַאי בָּצֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case behind רב פפא's reading in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פסח the dough always separates and the bowl stays pure. During the year the dough separates only if the owner is מקפיד; otherwise it is part of the bowl and transmits טומאה to it.

steps.title: New משנה: deaf dough
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that בצק החרש (dough with no visible signs of leavening) is forbidden if similar dough made at the same time has become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Deaf dough: if there is dough like it that has become leavened, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new משנה about a new topic: dough whose leavening cannot be seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Deaf' dough shows no signs, just as a deaf person gives no response. We cannot tell by looking whether it has become חמץ. So we compare it to dough that was made at the same time. If that dough has leavened, we assume this one has too.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Deaf dough: dough that shows no signs of leavening
Something like it; dough made at the same time and in the same way
Became leavened (חמץ)

phrases.english: Mishnah: Deaf dough,
if there is dough like it that became leavened,
this one is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בָּצֵק הַחֵרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic, unrelated to the עריבה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deaf dough is forbidden if comparable dough has become חמץ.

steps.title: What if there is no comparable dough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the rule is when there is no similar dough to compare with.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If there is no dough like it there, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a gap in the משנה and asks how to judge deaf dough when there is nothing to compare it to. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's test only works if a comparison dough exists. Without one, we need a different measure to know when the dough is presumed to be חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is it? (What is the law?)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אִם אֵין שָׁם כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Gemara: If there is no dough like it there, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵין שָׁם כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case the משנה in Step 9 left open.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to judge deaf dough when there is no comparison dough.

steps.title: The time to walk a מיל
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoted by רבי אבהו, answers that dough becomes חמץ in the time it takes to walk a מיל, the distance from מגדל נוניא to טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said that רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: The time it takes a person to walk from מגדל נוניא to טבריא, a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a set amount of time. Once that time passes, the dough is treated as חמץ even without a comparison dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With nothing to compare to, we use a time measure instead. The measure is the time it takes to walk one מיל (2000 אמות), shown by a known local distance. In practice, this time is commonly applied as about 18 minutes.

keyTerms.meaning: A distance of 2000 אַמּוֹת; also the time it takes to walk it
A town near טבריא; the name means 'tower of fish'
Tiberias

steps.whatToRemember: Without a comparison dough, deaf dough is presumed to be חמץ once the time of walking a מיל has passed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that dough becomes חמץ within the time of a מיל, the basis for timing in baking מצה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
The time it takes a person to walk
from Migdal Nunaya to Tiberias, a mil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Use a time measure: the time of walking a מיל, the distance from מגדל נוניא to טבריא.

steps.title: Why not just say 'a מיל'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of ריש לקיש's answer: why mention two towns at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him just say 'a מיל'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of ריש לקיש's statement from Step 11. It asks why he described the time as 'from מגדל נוניא to טבריא' instead of simply saying 'a מיל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש already said 'a מיל', so adding the two towns looks like extra, unneeded words. The גמרא assumes every word in a teaching is there for a reason, so it asks what the extra words add.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him say (instead).
A unit of distance, 2,000 אמות. Here it is used as a measure of time: how long it takes to walk that far.

phrases.english: Let him say 'a mil'!
phrases.notes: Why add the names of the towns?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא מִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of ריש לקיש's answer in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'from מגדל נוניא to טבריא' in ריש לקיש's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'a מיל' would have been enough, so the place names look unnecessary.

steps.title: The towns teach the length of a מיל
steps.stepSummary: The place names teach a second fact: a מיל is the distance from מגדל נוניא to טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that the length of a מיל is like the distance from מגדל נוניא to טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the place names are not extra. They teach us how long a מיל is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש taught two things at once: the rule about dough, and the length of a מיל, using a route people knew well. So the extra words carry new information.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us. A standard way the גמרא shows that seemingly extra words add something new.
The measure or size of something.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that the measure of a mil
is like from Migdal Nunaya to Tiberias.
phrases.notes: A well-known route, used as a real-life example of a מיל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the extra words teach something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The place names seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They define how long a מיל is.

steps.title: Four מילין for kneading, תפלה, and נטילת ידים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that one must go up to four מילין to find water for kneading in purity, for תפלה, and for נטילת ידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: for a kneader, for תפלה, and for washing hands, the measure is four מילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of ריש לקיש that also uses walking distance as a measure. A person must go as far as four מילין to find water before kneading, praying, or eating bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new rule, connected to the earlier one only because both use walking distance as a measure. The point is how much effort is required: if water can be reached within four מילין, you must go and get it, and if it is farther, you do not have to.

keyTerms.meaning: A kneader of dough, who must keep the dough ritually pure.
Prayer (שמונה עשרה). One washes hands before it.
Washing hands, for example before eating bread.
Four מילין, which is 8,000 אמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
phrases.notes: The same pair of names as in Step 11.

phrases.english: For a kneader, and for prayer,
and for washing hands,
the measure is four mil.
phrases.notes: This is how far one must go to find water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching from the same speakers that also uses a walking-distance measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For kneading in purity, for תפלה, and for נטילת ידים, one must go up to four מילין to find water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule about how far a person must go to find water to wash before תפלה or before eating bread.

steps.title: איבו taught it with a fourth case: tanning
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reports that איבו taught this teaching with four cases, and one of them was tanning hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: איבו said this teaching, and he said it about four cases, and one of them was tanning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different version of who said the teaching. He says איבו taught it, and listed four cases, not three; the fourth is tanning a hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things change here: who said it, and how many cases there are. The fourth case, tanning, is the amount of treading on a hide equal to walking four מילין. The next steps will prove this from a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא named איבו.
Tanning, the process that turns a raw hide into leather.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Ayvu said it,
and he said four cases in it,
and one of them is tanning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אַיְיבוּ אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of Step 14's teaching: a different speaker and a fourth case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four-מיל measure also applies to tanning hides.

steps.title: The משנה about tanned skins
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that skins become pure once tanned, or once trodden on long enough to count as tanning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: all these skins, if one tanned them, or walked on them long enough to tan them, are pure, except for human skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show where tanning has a set measure. The משנה mentions treading on a hide 'enough for tanning', and this is the measure איבו meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some soft skins count like flesh for טומאה. Once they are tanned, or walked on enough to equal tanning, they become leather and are pure. Human skin is the exception and stays impure. The phrase 'enough for tanning' needs a measure, which the next steps supply.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough for tanning, meaning the amount of treading that equals tanning.
Human skin.

steps.confusionAlert: 'הִילֵּךְ בָּהֶן' here means treading or walking on the hide itself. It is not about walking somewhere to look for water.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
And all of them (these skins) that one tanned,
phrases.notes: Skins that count like flesh for טומאה.

phrases.english: or that one walked on them enough for tanning,
are pure,
except for human skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן וְכוּלָּן שֶׁעִיבְּדָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for איבו's fourth case, tanning.
steps.raayaObject: That tanning has a set walking-based measure, as איבו said.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about skins that become pure through tanning or treading.

steps.title: How much treading counts as tanning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long one must tread on a hide to equal tanning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'enough for tanning'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the measure behind the משנה's words 'enough for tanning'. This question sets up the answer that links back to four מילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives no number. The answer will show that the measure is four מילין, which completes איבו's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is 'enough for tanning'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה כְּדֵי עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure of the משנה's phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact measure of 'enough for tanning'.

steps.title: Enough to walk four מילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי איבו, quoting רבי ינאי, rules that tanning requires as much treading as walking four מילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי איבו said in the name of רבי ינאי: as much as walking four מילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that treading on a hide for the length of a four-מיל walk counts as tanning. This confirms that tanning is the fourth four-מיל case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the proof is complete. The משנה's phrase 'enough for tanning' equals four מילין of walking, so איבו was right to add tanning to the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking.

phrases.english: Rabbi (Ayvu) said that Rabbi Yannai said:
phrases.notes: The name in round brackets is how the standard printed גמרא has it, but it isn't certain; some versions read it as איבו.

phrases.english: The amount of walking four mil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי (אִינְיָיא) אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Enough for tanning means treading as long as it takes to walk four מילין.

steps.title: Four מילין only when the water is ahead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא limits the four-מיל rule to water that lies ahead of the traveler.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: they taught this only about water in front of him. But if the water is behind him, he does not go back even a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the rule about going for water before תפלה or eating. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the four-מיל rule applies only to water ahead on your path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going forward is on your way, so we ask more of you. Turning back costs more, so a traveler is not required to go back as far as a מיל for water behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... A standard phrase for limiting a rule.
In front of him, on his way.
Behind him.
Goes back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
They taught this only when it is in front of him,
phrases.notes: The water is ahead, in the direction he is traveling.

phrases.english: but behind him,
he does not go back even a mil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the water rule of Step 14 and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four מילין applies only to water ahead; for water behind, one need not go back a מיל.

steps.title: Less than a מיל behind, he must go back
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא infers that a traveler must go back for water if it is less than a מיל behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said: we learn from this that only a full מיל is too far to go back. If it is less than a מיל, he does go back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא reads closely what רבי יוסי said and draws a practical rule from it. Since only a full מיל is too far, water less than a מיל behind you must still be fetched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said 'not even a מיל', which implies that something less than a מיל is different. This gives the full rule: ahead, up to four מילין; behind, less than one מיל.

keyTerms.meaning: And from this (we can learn).
Less than a מיל.

steps.whatToRemember: How far to go for water to wash before תפלה or eating: up to four מילין if the water is ahead of you; if it is behind you, go back only if it is less than one מיל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard rule of how much effort a traveler must make to wash his hands.

phrases.english: Rav Acha said: and from this we learn:
It is a full mil that he does not go back,
but less than a mil, he does go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא וּמִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implied rule from רבי יוסי's wording in Step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For water behind you, you must go back if it is less than a מיל.

steps.title: How is impure חלה separated on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how one separates חלה from impure dough on יום טוב of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How do we separate חלה when the dough is impure, on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens by asking a practical question. It is setting up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure חלה cannot be eaten by a כהן, so it must be burned. Burning it on יום טוב is forbidden, because it is not food anyone may eat. But leaving the raw dough until after יום טוב is also a problem, because it will turn into חמץ during פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the text the גמרא will discuss
How? In what way?
The portion of dough that must be given to a כהן
In a state of ritual impurity
The festival day, here the first day of פסח

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether to separate חלה. It must be separated. The question is how to do it when the חלה is impure and can neither be burned nor left alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole משנה is a search for a way out of this trap: the חלה cannot be burned on יום טוב, and it cannot be allowed to become חמץ.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: How does one separate חלה
in impurity on the Festival day?
phrases.notes: The dough is טמא, so the חלה will need to be burned

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד מַפְרִישִׁין חַלָּה בְּטוּמְאָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not connect to the earlier discussion of four מילין and traveling for water (steps 14–20).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A method for separating impure חלה on יום טוב of פסח that avoids both burning it on יום טוב and letting it become חמץ.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: wait until the dough is baked
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says not to designate the חלה until after the dough is baked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: She should not give it the name חלה until it is baked.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the first answer: bake all the dough first, and only then separate the חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baked bread can no longer become חמץ. So if she separates the חלה only after baking, she can simply set it aside and burn it after יום טוב. This avoids both problems.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not give it a name, meaning do not designate it as חלה
Until it is baked

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
She should not call it by name [as חלה]
phrases.notes: She should not designate the חלה while the dough is still raw

phrases.english: until it is baked.
phrases.notes: Once it is baked it cannot become חמץ, so it can wait until after יום טוב

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר לֹא תִּקְרָא לָהּ שֵׁם עַד שֶׁתֵּאָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the משנה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Delay designating the חלה until after baking. Baked dough cannot become חמץ, so the חלה can be kept and burned after יום טוב.

steps.title: בן בתירא: put it in cold water
steps.stepSummary: בן בתירא says to separate the חלה right away and put it in cold water so it will not become חמץ. The משנה then begins to introduce רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן בתירא says: She should put it in cold water. רבי יהושע said:
steps.whatsHappening: בן בתירא gives a second answer: separate the חלה now and keep it in cold water. The last words, "רבי יהושע said," set up a third opinion that continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר avoids the problem by delaying the separation. בן בתירא instead separates the חלה immediately and stops it from turning into חמץ, because cold water slows the dough from rising. Either way, the חלה is kept from becoming חמץ until it can be burned after יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: She should place it or throw it
In cold water

steps.confusionAlert: "אמר רבי יהושע" is only the opening of רבי יהושע's statement. His actual view comes on the next amud. It is not part of בן בתירא's opinion.

phrases.english: Ben Beteira says:
She should place it in cold water.
phrases.notes: Cold water keeps the separated dough from becoming חמץ

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
phrases.notes: Introduces the next opinion, which continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר תָּטִיל בְּצוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different solution from רבי אליעזר's, and then opens רבי יהושע's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Separate the חלה before baking and keep it in cold water so it does not become חמץ before it can be burned after יום טוב.
